questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Japan offered a completely new perspective on academic life and the future career opportunities. Meanwhile, the culture itself had many depths to delve into and experience. Something that is only possible by extensive cultural contact.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The SKP-staff and university personel in general were impeccable in providing information - perhaps to a fault. Be ware of the risk of information overload and use your peers to navigate the sometimes Kafkaesque bureaucratic systems of Japan.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The orientation day along with study guide sent out beforehand had ample information to get through the first days of arrival.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Use the dorms offered to international students if you don't mind some mess and questionable hygiene.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is the norm. Most Japanese still live their parents while most international students live off campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The lottery system was a bit of surprise! Make sure you have enough eligible courses at university by a wide margin before you apply.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Online with parallel processes. Make sure to apply for language courses before arriving and getting positive confirmation, once you're there its too late to apply for these.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Kind support via email or open office hours.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had a great deal of luck securing the classes i applied for, but they were not entirely the ones I had thought about before applying for exchange. The courses will change depending on many factors. Don't be too set in your expectations.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be prepared to not get all your prioty courses and perhaps even not at the campus nearest you.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The English proficiency of not only the students but the lecturers leaned more towards BA-level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More focus on individual performance and experiences, almost no group work, and many classes had attendance. Meaning, the trust between students and teachers were not as high.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Just make sure to have a variety of evaluation goals - check the course descriptions - most have a final paper and these have to be handed in the same week of the semester. Try to spread it out.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not many. Some deposits and bureaucratic stuff. Mostly you get it back at the end of the semester.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Since the JPY was historically low, most things were pretty cheap. Although, fresh produce - fruits and veggies - are expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They have whole program for clubs and circles that you can join without having to speak much Japanese, just beware that you will have to dedicate yourself and your time to them, so you will have to choose.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't join any.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Just go take the train somewhere - there are too many places to visit and the months will quickly pass. Even just taking the bike or the bus to a famous temple or nice ramen place a day after class will make for time well spent.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Difficult. Japanese people have little time for socialising. So ask the people with knowledge on the subject. They are also used to large-scale tourism and foreigners being "baka" (stupid), so don't worry too much. But be nice and humble and they will respect you - to an extent.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The individualism hidden behind the extremely considerate facade. Loneliness and heavy workloads everywhere - people sleeping in public transport and libraries.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Overall friendliness and accomodating atmosphere.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Learn the language. Every experience is better shared. Look for adventure, but remember to consider your inner balance.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The course lottery system!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Finding friends and relationships beyond cultures and even languages.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Striking a balance between solitude and social activities.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
